differences.what: the pedestal's front and west faces: the base, plinth and die at the camera's fourteen fitted corners, 10.5 px rms, the largest residual 22 px (0.1 m) on the mouldings

the pedestal's depths: the west faces show the base 2.85 m, the plinth 1.8 m and the die 1.6 m deep; built 3.3, 2.3 and 1.9 m (reconstructed) until this camera measured them [T-3568: the record's depths set to the reading and the monument rebuilt]
the die's west panel, a narrow bronze plate on the west face: drawn in the render in place
the cap's profile: two stepped washes and a fillet in the print, one slab over a cove in the render, its overhang within 0.15 m
the plinth's top moulding and the die's base moulding: drawn in more steps in the print than the render's single fillet, under 0.1 m
the front panel's tone: fresh dark bronze, darker than the new granite, in this 1893 print, as the render draws it
the lettering under the front panel, three lines of pale cut letters: not cut in the render

the warrior (left): in the print he lunges to the left, crouched, his weight on a bent right leg with the left stretched back, his body twisted toward the woman and his head at Black Partridge's shoulder, the tomahawk raised over his head in his right hand and a feather in his hair; the render stands him upright on straight legs, so his head and the tomahawk's head stand about 0.35-0.4 m higher than the sculpture's and his stride is lost

Margaret Helm (centre): in the print she staggers, leaning back against Black Partridge, her head turned, her right arm reaching across to the warrior, her dress falling in folds to the rock with a cloak loose behind; the render is an upright figure in a smooth cone of skirt with her arms out to the sides

Black Partridge (behind her, right): in the print his left arm is raised high and out to the upper left with the palm open against the blow, his head in a headdress with a long feather streaming back, the musket slanting down past his right side; the render raises a straight arm ending in a long bar and carries a stick at his right, without the open hand, the headdress or the musket's shape

the post surgeon (under them): in the print he lies across the front of the rock under the woman's skirt, his legs out toward the child; the render is a low lump with a ball for a head at the woman's left
the child (right front): in the print he kneels at the rock's right edge reaching out with both arms; the render stands him upright in a cone with one arm out
the rock: a rough, broken mound rising under the figures' feet in the picture; a low smooth swell in the render
the faces, hair, dress and undress, ornaments and weapons as sculpted: not modelled (the figures are joined from tapered limbs and balls, L-fort-dearborn-monument-3567)

the group's outline as a whole: the print's rises from the rock at about y 690 to the tomahawk at y 175 (orig. px) and spans x 350-830; the render's spans x 330-900 and its tomahawk stands at y 135, the warrior's upright stance and Black Partridge's long bar (above)
the estate wall and its coped pier behind at right, and the young street tree: not drawn by this review
